problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)={e}^{2t+1}.$ At time $t=0.5$ the particle is located at the position $x={e}^{2}.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=2?$

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=3{e}^{3t-1}.$ At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=2{e}^{2}.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=5?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=5$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,5].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(5)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{5}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(5) & =2{e}^{2}+{\int }_{1}^{5}3{e}^{3t-1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{e}^{2}+{[{e}^{3t-1}]}_{1}^{5} \\  & =2{e}^{2}+({e}^{3(5)-1}-{e}^{3(1)-1}) \\  & =2{e}^{2}+({e}^{14}-{e}^{2}) \\  & =2{e}^{2}+{e}^{14}-{e}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2}+{e}^{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=5$ is $x={e}^{2}+{e}^{14}.$
